entity.summary: Major U.S.-origin centralized cryptocurrency exchange within the Coinbase group. Coinbase remained active after the 2025 dismissal of the SEC civil action and expanded its regulated European structure when Coinbase Luxembourg S.A. received MiCA authorization in June 2025.
entity.notes: The 2012 marker follows the broader Coinbase platform lineage; the dedicated institutional Coinbase Exchange product evolved through later Coinbase Exchange / GDAX branding. The Luxembourg MiCA authorization is scoped to Coinbase Luxembourg S.A. and EEA-facing regulated services, not every Coinbase product worldwide. Existing 2023 SEC action and 2025 dismissal events are not duplicated.

expected.summary: Major U.S.-based centralized cryptocurrency exchange. HEI records Coinbase as an active exchange with event-backed history, including a 2023 SEC civil action and the 2025 dismissal of that action.

events.title: Coinbase announced Luxembourg MiCA authorization
events.description: Coinbase announced that Coinbase Luxembourg S.A. had received authorization from Luxembourg's CSSF as a crypto-asset service provider under MiCA, supporting regulated service provision across the EU and EEA through the Luxembourg entity.
events.notes: The event date follows Coinbase's public announcement. Authorization scope is limited to the Luxembourg entity and its regulated European services.

events.title: X named Coinbase a U.S. Cashtag launch partner
events.description: X launched its U.S. Cashtag Partner Program with Coinbase among the initial brokerage and exchange partners, adding a Trade route from supported Cashtag asset pages to Coinbase where users complete transactions on the partner platform.
events.notes: This is a distribution/access-channel event, not an HEI status change. X routes users to the partner platform and does not execute the trade itself. HEI attaches the Coinbase partnership to the existing Coinbase Exchange umbrella entity rather than creating a separate Coinbase.com entity.

events.title: Coinbase opened IPO allocations to eligible U.S. retail customers
events.description: Coinbase began allowing eligible U.S. retail customers to request IPO share allocations through its app, starting with Oura's IPO. Securities are offered through FINRA-registered broker-dealer Coinbase Capital Markets, and final allocations depend on selling-group supply and customer demand.
events.notes: This records a major product and market-access expansion into primary-market securities, not an HEI status change. Allocation requests are not guaranteed and may be filled in full, in part, or not at all. Securities services provided by Coinbase Capital Markets are separate from Coinbase Inc. digital-asset services.

evidence.title: Coinbase Secures MiCA Licence: A Milestone in Europe’s Crypto Evolution
evidence.notes: First-party announcement of the Luxembourg MiCA authorization and European hub structure.

evidence.title: MiCA authorization and changes to Coinbase service
evidence.notes: Current first-party service notice identifying Coinbase Luxembourg S.A. and the MiCA authorization.

evidence.title: X launches U.S. Cashtag Program with brokerage partners
evidence.notes: First-party X announcement for the U.S. Cashtag Partner Program naming Coinbase among the launch partners and describing the Trade handoff to participating brokerages.

evidence.title: X will now let US users trade via Cashtags
evidence.notes: Independent reporting corroborates Coinbase as an initial Cashtag partner and clarifies that users continue to the participating brokerage or exchange to complete the transaction.

evidence.title: You can now participate in IPOs on Coinbase
evidence.notes: First-party announcement confirming U.S. retail IPO allocation access through the Coinbase app, beginning with Oura, and identifying Coinbase Capital Markets as the FINRA-registered broker-dealer providing the securities access.

evidence.title: Coinbase opens IPO allocations to US customers, starting with Oura
evidence.notes: Independent reporting corroborates the U.S. retail launch, Oura as the first IPO, offer-price requests, non-guaranteed allocations, and Coinbase's broader expansion beyond crypto into traditional-market products.
